chapter_theme: Having love (அன்புடைமை): love and Siva are not two; austerity without melting love cannot reach him, but he stands in the love of those who praise him, dwells within love, and is the near support of those who live in it.
structure_note: The thesis that love is Siva (270); the poet's own love and its answer (271, 274, 275); love against austerity (272) and against mere desire (278); Siva within love (276, 277, 279).

270.reading: The ignorant say love and Siva are two; no one knows that love itself is Siva; once they know it, they rest as love that is Siva.
270.nuance: அன்பே சிவம் is the verse's refrain and one of the best-known lines in Tamil. The last line makes knowing it transformative: those who know do not merely hold a doctrine but sit (அமர்ந்திருந்தார்) as that love.

271.reading: My great love is entwined with the one who wears the tiger skin that outshines gold, with the young crescent gleaming like lightning, who bathes in the ash heaped close about him.
271.nuance: The tiger skin, crescent and burning-ground ash (சுடுபொடி) are Siva's standard marks. கிடந்து runs through the lines, so the love lies close to him as the skin, moon and ash do.

272.reading: Even if one makes one's bones the firewood, cuts one's flesh and fries it in the fire till it glows like gold, none but those who melt with love and soften within can reach my gem.
272.nuance: The extreme of bodily austerity is set aside in favour of love that melts (உருகி) and softens (குழை). என்போல் மணி is unclear: 'my gem' or 'the gem that is like me'.

273.reading: Those with longing see Hara, those with tenderness see his feet, but those who carry a burden see only birth, as if they had taken a harsh road into Kongu.
273.nuance: ஆர்வம், ஈரம், பாரம் rhyme as three states of the heart; பாரம் is taken as the weight of attachment or deeds, and பவம் as birth. Line 4 (கோர நெறிகொடு கொங்குபுக்காரே) is obscure: கொங்கு may be the Kongu country, or honey.

274.reading: Melt your love and praise the Lord; melt your love first and seek the First One; when I later melted with love, great Nandi made his love for me stand foremost.
274.nuance: என் அன்பு, முன் அன்பு, பின் அன்பு, தன் அன்பு move from the hearer's love to the Lord's answering love. Nandi is Tirumular's teacher and also a name of Siva; the verse need not choose.

275.reading: Even if one praises him only once as the self-born, he stands then as a companion on the way to heaven; Siva, wearing the konrai with honey on one side, stood in my love in a way all his own.
275.nuance: ஒரு runs through the lines (ஒரு காலம், ஒரு பால், ஒரு வண்ணம்): a single praise is enough to make him a companion. சயம்பு is svayambhu, the self-born.

276.reading: People do not know how to hold with love our Lord, the First who first created and created joy; yet he who locked love into life in this wide world stays in his own wide realm.
276.nuance: அடைத்து (locking in, enclosing) is used twice: people fail to enclose the Lord in love, while he enclosed love in the world. வன்படைத்து and the second அகலிடம் are unclear.

277.reading: If one sets in the mind the Lord who shines like the sun of fine red gold, keeps him there, praises him as Lord and seeks his grace with longing, the king of the gods grants increase.
277.nuance: அருத்தி is longing or devotion. விருத்தி can be growth, livelihood or, in later usage, growth in grace; the verse does not say which.

278.reading: Though they know the order set by the one who made daily sleep and birth, men keep him within their wants, calling him 'our father, our Lord', and do not seek him with longing.
278.nuance: நித்தலும் துஞ்சும் பிறப்பு may be 'daily sleep and birth' or 'the birth that daily dies'; sleep as a small death is an old figure (Kural 339). The complaint is that people call on the Lord for what they want (இச்சை) rather than out of love for him (நச்சி).

279.reading: He is within love and outside it, within the body, before and after, lord even of the sages; the rare being who dwells within love is a close support only to those who dwell in love.
279.nuance: அன்பின் உள் occurs four times. The Lord is everywhere (inside, outside, before, after), yet his nearness as support (அணைதுணை) is given only to those in love.

links.note: Both correct what 'the ignorant' (அறியார், அறிவிலார்) say about love: the Kural that love serves not only virtue but also against wrong, Tirumular that love is not a second thing beside Siva. Each widens love past a limit set on it.

Both join bones, burning and love. In the Kural virtue scorches the loveless as the sun a boneless worm; in Tirumular a man burns his own bones and flesh, and without love it still does not reach God.
270 says love is Siva; 279 spells out what follows: he dwells within love and is close support only to those who dwell in it.

source_issues: 276: line 3 (வன்படைத்து இந்த அகலிடம் வாழ்வினில்) is unclear.
